materialDissent: Semantic split for one user-visible condition: waiting on Jira search-index lag exits 20 from the pre-mutation duplicate gate, but stays exit 2 from submit's retry-verification-interval wait and exits 0 from explicit `reconcile --verify`. The packet documents this as deliberate/out-of-scope, and I accept it for this change, but I do not agree it is cost-free: the stated purpose of code 20 is to let a caller distinguish a transient, retry-after-lag block from a genuine state error, and that affordance is only partially delivered. A caller implementing `retry on 20` will silently fail to retry the retry-verification wait, which is the same class of transient wait.

Backward-compatibility judgment: moving a case that previously surfaced as exit 2 to exit 20 is a change to a shipped, documented CLI exit-code contract. The repo-internal audit is now conclusive that no in-repo consumer breaks, and 20 is fail-safe for any generic `code !== 0` handler — but it is NOT fail-safe for an out-of-repo consumer that matches `code === 2` explicitly and treats anything else as unexpected. The packet treats this residual as closed-by-disclosure; I treat it as accepted-risk-by-owner-decision, which is a different thing. No version bump or changelog entry accompanies the contract change (package.json remains kstack@0.1.0).
review.recommendation: Approve and ship as-is. The round-15 failedCheck is genuinely closed: the broken `\\(spawn\\|exec\\)` ERE pattern was reproduced and proven to match only literal text before the corrected grouped pattern was relied on, scope is now unrestricted repo-wide (401 files, hidden/ignored/untracked included, only .git and node_modules excluded), every package-manager alias form and every process-launch API actually present in the tree is covered, and the numeric `== 2` comparison scan plus the whole-file invocation/status-idiom intersection both come back with live matches that were individually inspected and are non-consumers. Behavior is unchanged for every path except the three intended call sites; the null-vs-0 refactor of youngestMarkerAgeMs is strictly conservative (unmeasurable, negative, and non-finite ages all still block, now with a distinct audit reason), and the no-marker Infinity case still clears as before. Two optional, non-blocking follow-ups for a later change, not this one: (1) collapse the reason asymmetry so the gate's return sentinel and the audit record use one value for one condition, or add a comment at gateExitCode explaining why VERIFICATION_REASON.INDEX_LAG is a return-channel-only value that never appears in an audit record; (2) if code 20 is ever intended to drive automated retry, extend it to submit's retry-verification wait so the retry affordance is complete, and bump the package version / add a changelog line since the exit-code contract is now documented and consumed externally.
review.strongestObjection: VERIFICATION_REASON.INDEX_LAG is a sentinel that exists only on the gate's return value and is never written to any audit record, while the audit entry for that exact same condition writes MARKER_YOUNGER_THAN_INDEX_LAG_MINIMUM. So the on-disk audit trail and the exit code are driven by two different strings for one condition, coupled only by the ordering of the two statements inside preMutationDuplicateGate. Nothing structural enforces that coupling: a future edit that normalizes the audit reason, or that reuses VERIFICATION_REASON.INDEX_LAG in a queueAudit call, will decouple exit code from audit evidence, and the operator-facing story ("exit 20 means the audit says index lag") becomes wrong. Current tests pin the exit code and the audit reason independently, so they would catch a mismatch today, but they do not encode the invariant itself. This is a maintenance hazard rather than a defect — it is my strongest objection precisely because every behavioral objection from rounds 11-15 is now resolved with fresh, self-verified evidence.
unresolvedQuestions: The repo-wide audit conclusively covers branching on exit codes, but the change also introduces a new audit `reason` value (`marker-age-unmeasurable`) replacing what was previously recorded as `marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum` for unparseable/future/non-finite marker ages. No scan in this packet establishes that nothing reads or asserts on audit `reason` strings outside the updated test file. In-repo this is almost certainly safe (tests were updated and pass), but the same out-of-repo residual that applies to exit codes applies to audit reasons, and it has not been separately disclosed.

This is the single concrete item keeping me at 95 rather than higher: whether any out-of-repo installation of this plugin matches exit code 2 exactly (as opposed to `code !== 0`). It is unobservable by any repository-internal search, so it cannot be closed by more grep evidence — it can only be closed by an owner statement that no external exit-2-specific consumer exists, or by treating the change as a deliberate, version-flagged contract break.
